newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Petronas to get same terms as BHP in Dai Hung field.
newsitem.headline: Petronas to get same terms as BHP in Dai Hung field.

text.p: Malaysia's Petronas would get the same contract terms as The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd if it took over the Australian firm's stake in Vietnam's Dai Hung oil field, Petrovietnam said on Wednesday.
"We would have the same production-sharing contract," the state oil and gas firm's President, Ngo Thuong San, told reporters at an energy industry fair.
He said an application by Petronas, the Malaysian state-owned oil firm, to buy out BHP's 43.75 percent stake was currently in the hands of the Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI).
Petronas already has a 20-percent stake in the field. Petrovietnam has 15 percent while France's Total SA and Japan's Sumitomo Corp have 10.625 percent each.
Petronas officials said earlier this month that they were optimistic about the field's prospects despite BHP's decision to divest its stake.

BHP has given up on the field due to disagreements with the Vietnamese government over taxes applying to the field, which contains less oil than was forecast at the time the tax system was formulated.
Since BHP bought into the field in April 1993, estimates of reserves have been slashed to about 100 million barrels from up to 800 million.
K.C. Singh, head of Petronas' exploration operations in Vietnam, told Reuters that his company did not expect a new contract to be drawn up. He expected a decision from the MPI by the end of May.
San said Petrovietnam could also take some of BHP's stake.
"We are now discussing with Petronas about Petrovietnam taking a share," he said, without elaborating.
